task: open-tennis-robots: edge-time drop fit, whole-drill check (flagship buildable item)

doc_friction.issue: Two sessions took the same buildable item (edge-time fit) within the hour: claim_check works per flagship and item, but #16574 had bundled the item into an ESC-survey PR whose title named the ESC survey first, so the claim read as free.

deviations.why: No llms.txt or marketing page change: the work is a firmware estimator option that is off by default, nothing user-facing changed.

goal: Test whether fitting the loop-command drop on tach edge times (running sums) beats the period fit under tach jitter.
notes: Duplicate work: PR #16574 landed the same edge-time option (off) while this session built its own. On merging main this session took main's controller and kept only what was new: tests/edge_fit_drill.py (calibration drill, 18 builds x 3 seeds, swaps the board's fit for the edge form) and a README addendum. Whole drill spin rms periods -> edges: 2.20 -> 2.97% at 5 us jitter, 6.55 -> 9.07% at 10 us, 8.67 -> 9.06% at 80 ms ESC lag, 0.62 -> 0.58% first-order. Cause checks: period-row noise lag-1 corr -0.498; linear toy gain 4%; with the lag fixed and the noise added open loop the sums still read worse, which points at t0. Verification: run_venture_tests.py open-tennis-robots ok (328 tests, 0 failed) and venture-preflight clean, both before the merge with main; after the merge only docs, an eval file and a standalone sweep script differ from main.
